| [0010](./0010/) | core | draft | major | not-started | 2026-07-31 — The migration inventory's central finding CORRECTED on author input, and the collection gap CLOSED BY DATA. The fleet does not resolve through CUE's default central registry — it resolves against ghcr.io/open-platform-model, and the reason the operator Deployment shows no registry configuration is that it needs none: opm-operator/cmd/main.go:94-98 gives the --registry flag a COMPILED-IN DEFAULT of 'testing.opmodel.dev=ghcr.io/open-platform-model,opmodel.dev=ghcr.io/open-platform-model,registry.cue.works'. The 2026-07-30 observations were all accurate (no env, no arg, no mounted config, verified again 2026-07-31 including envFrom); only the inference from them was wrong, and nothing in the cluster object could have shown otherwise because the value is in the binary. GHCR enumerates completely through gh api --paginate: 53 packages, recorded as inventory section 3b, and EVERY live coordinate is present at its deployed version — including all three modules the workspace registry lacks entirely, radarr/sabnzbd/sonarr each carrying v1.0.0-v1.0.2. So the gap that gated SCHEDULING the migration is closed, and the draft->accepted inventory gate is now satisfied by data rather than by a stated absence. The two-registry finding SURVIVES and remains operative — the registries are neither subset nor superset, 74 repositories locally against 53 packages on GHCR — it simply constrains the runbook instead of blocking it from being written. THREE DEFECTS SHRANK on the same read. The opm_experimental spelling collision is WORSE than recorded in one respect and unchanged in kind: both spellings are published to GHCR as well as to localhost:5000, so the canonicalisation is a two-registry deletion. opmodel.dev/modules/opm-platform is ABSENT from GHCR, existing only on localhost:5000 alongside the library/testdata fixture, so both are dev-registry hygiene rather than wrong inputs to a fleet migration. And the source-tree/registry reconciliation loses most of its content, since radarr, sabnzbd and sonarr are published on GHCR at exactly their deployed v1.0.2, leaving only cdi and snapshot_controller sourced-but-unpublished-anywhere. 04-graduation records all three as cleanup rather than as gates. TWO NEW FINDINGS, neither predicted. resolveRegistry (main.go:334-342) documents its precedence as --registry > OPM_REGISTRY > CUE's built-in default and returns the flag value whenever it is non-empty; because the flag's default IS non-empty, both lower tiers are UNREACHABLE — setting OPM_REGISTRY on the operator does nothing, and CUE's own resolution is never used, unless a caller passes --registry='' explicitly. That matters directly to the planned move, since retargeting the fleet needs the flag or a new default and not an environment variable. Second, opmodel.dev/modules/test/podinfo carries roughly SEVENTY -e2e.g<sha> prerelease tags in MODULE space — enhancement 0006 OQ18's dev-tag pollution in a namespace that entry did not examine; harmless under D14 since a platform names one build, but noise the 0011 D5 namespace move must carry or drop deliberately. RECORDED FOR SEQUENCING: a dedicated central registry on ZOT is planned to replace the GHCR arrangement. It changes nothing about what the migration does, since neither 0010's identity values nor 0011 D5's namespace depend on which host serves the bytes, but doing the namespace move into GHCR and then moving hosts pays the republish cost twice — the same argument that makes the joint 0010/0011 window a preference — so 06-operational says to sequence the two together or move hosts first, and marks it a scheduling decision owned by the Zot rollout rather than a design one. | Module and Catalog Identity |
| [0011](./0011/) | cli | draft | minor | not-started | 2026-07-31 — Three riders recorded from 0010's OQ walk, OQ9 filed, and a tooling defect fixed that had been hiding open questions. D9 GAINS A LEVEL-AWARE RIDER following 0010 D34: the compatibility gate reads each primitive's apiVersion and runs the pull-and-compare only at beta and GA, because D34 keys D27's promise to the level and an alpha contract may break freely. This is INHERITED rather than an amendment — D9 names D27 rather than restating it, so narrowing D27 narrows the gate automatically — but it is recorded because D9's own wording says 'every primitive in the tree' and an implementer would gate all of them. Two properties are unchanged: the apiVersion bump stays the escape hatch, since the lookup is keyed on name+apiVersion and a bumped contract finds no predecessor and passes trivially; and the MATCH-side rung does not skip alpha, so a removed field still fails loudly. What alpha gives up is exactly the default-drift class 0010/experiments/02 measured, confined under D34's day-one assignment to catalog_opm_experimental. D7 GAINS A COMPATIBILITY MODE following 0010 D35: `opm catalog registry check --compat` compares a published catalog against its predecessor under D9's rule, shipped explicitly as an AID rather than a gate — a distinction that belongs in the command's help text and not only in a design document, since D35 accepts publish-side enforcement as the whole of the guarantee. It reuses D9's comparator, so the marginal cost is plumbing. D5 GAINS A SCOPE LIMIT and OQ9 is filed: D5 partitions three artifact classes (m, catalogs, core) and the registry demonstrably holds more, measured rather than hypothesised — opmodel.dev/modules/opm-platform was a #Platform published into MODULE space at v1.0.0 and v1.0.1 while its own source header declares it an unpublished on-disk fixture, and opmodel.dev/releases/* holds four repositories of Instance-vocabulary artifacts under a segment D5 never reserved. Test fixtures are the useful precedent because they are already solved differently — by a separate DOMAIN, testing.opmodel.dev, mapped in every registry configuration in the workspace — which suggests the answer here may be a domain rather than a segment. OQ9's candidate (c), that platforms and instances are not published artifacts at all and both measured cases are defects, is the cheapest answer if it holds and the opm_platform header already asserts it for platforms. SEPARATELY, A TOOLING DEFECT: `task questions:open` parses the Status line up to the first period, so the form 'Status: open, filed <date>.' yields the literal string 'open, filed <date>' which matches no bucket and is silently OMITTED FROM THE QUEUE. Six Open Questions across four entries were invisible — 0011 OQ8 since 2026-07-30 and this entry's new OQ9, 0010 OQ16 and OQ17, 0012 OQ4 (which 0010 OQ10 was deferred to and whose own graduation gate makes answering mandatory), and 0006 OQ18. All were normalised to 'Status: open. Filed <date>.' except 0006's, that entry being implemented and therefore frozen. This matters beyond tidiness: an OQ the queue does not report is an OQ the promotion gate cannot see, and 0010 was briefly described as carrying no open questions on the strength of an empty queue. | Module and Catalog Publishing |

| [0013](./0013/) | cross-cutting | draft | - | not-started | 2026-07-27 — Design revised on review: D10 supersedes D1, D11 supersedes D4, D12 amends D9, and OQ1 is closed. D1 had removed the `#Secret` contract type AND the disjunction inside it, when only the routing metadata needed to move to the attribute — leaving the deployer no slot in which to say "this Secret already exists", and forcing the handle-plus-context-map machinery of D4 to compensate. D10 restores `#Secret` narrowed to `#SecretLiteral | #SecretRef`, so the ATTRIBUTE carries routing (author intent, static, in the published module) and the TYPE carries fulfilment (deployer choice, per environment, type-checked by CUE). D11 replaces handle substitution with resolve-in-place: the kernel rewrites every secret to its `#SecretRef` form, so both arms converge before render, a transformer reads two fields from one branch, and the whole handle format, the `#TransformerContext` addition, the `owned` flag and the output scanner are all deleted. Three properties fall out that the first draft lacked: instance files for supplied secrets do not change at all, plaintext in the render is structurally unrepresentable rather than stripped, and a secret interpolated into a rendered string fails at plain `cue vet` at authoring time. Experiment 02 rebuilt as `02-resolve-in-place` and re-run: all five claims held, and its Go content hash agrees with the CUE one in examples.cue. OQ2 opened — whether the arm rewrite survives the real kernel build path — and is now the sole blocker to acceptance. | Attribute-Declared Secret Fields |
| [0014](./0014/) | cli | draft | none | not-started | 2026-07-29 — Drafted. 0006 shipped the handoff that moves an instance's manager to the operator; nothing moves its definition out of the cluster, so a CLI-first user who now wants GitOps hand-assembles four YAML documents per instance from a `kubectl get -o yaml` dump. Three decisions came from the user on the day: the exported unit is the CR plus its apply envelope rather than a bare CR (D1), export refuses to write unless the published module reproduces `status.lastAppliedRenderDigest` (D2, reusing handoff's gate chain and `VerificationDigest`), and `spec.values` is written verbatim with a warning rather than redacted or refused, because OPM cannot yet identify which values are secret (D3). D4 records the live CR as the sole input. Two findings from reading the code shaped the design. `ApplySpec` (cli/internal/inventory/store.go:119) writes only `spec.module`, `spec.owner`, and `spec.values`, so every CLI-written CR lacks `spec.serviceAccountName` and `spec.prune` — meaning a dump-and-strip export applies under the controller's own identity and orphans its workloads on delete, a behaviour difference invisible in the YAML. And the render-bearing / apply-bearing partition resolves the tension that finding creates: the fields the digest gate verifies are copied untouched, while the fields governing apply identity and deletion sit outside the render digest and can be completed without weakening the guarantee, provided every completion is reported. The partition is enforced in schemas/target.cue rather than asserted in prose. Six open questions; OQ4 (field-manager collision when Flux's kustomize-controller applies over fields owned by opm-cli and the operator) is the load-bearing one and is gated on a runnable experiment, because it decides whether the adoption is as quiet as D2's guarantee implies. | Export a Deployed Instance as GitOps Manifests |

- **draft** — initial design, actively being written
- **accepted** — design agreed upon, ready for implementation
- **implemented** — design has been realized in code
- **superseded** — replaced by a newer enhancement (see `superseded_by` in the entry's config.yaml)
